Niger — 18th-highest-population country, and the first this round where the fallback-to-national-tier rule was forced rather than optional: Niamey has been run by a CNSP-appointed Administrateur Délégué (not an elected mayor) since the 2023 coup, and its own municipal portal confirms this while publishing zero fiscal documents. `af-waemu-remainder.json` already covers Niger's IHPC (ne-ins-ihpc) including its IMF CPI Manual 2020 citation; this round adds the commune legal-fiscal framework, a WAEMU financial-regime instrument Niger's own MOF republishes, an AFRISTAT linkage in INS Niger's own voice, and the AES/ECOWAS-withdrawal thread in Niger's Ministry of Finance's own words.

reports.title: Ordonnance n°2010-54 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales du Niger
reports.description: Niger's general code of territorial collectivités, verified via a Niger-government-authored primary text (hosted on WHO's extranet legal repository, corroborated by an identical copy on UEMOA's own document repository, orfao.uemoa.int). Art. 20: "La commune assure les services publics répondant aux besoins de la population et qui ne relèvent pas...de l'Etat ou de la région. Elle jouit de la personnalité morale et de l'autonomie financière." Art. 30 gives the commune fiscal/budgetary competence: "budgets et comptes; création d'impôts et taxes rémunératoires conformément aux dispositions de la loi des finances; fixation des taux des impôts et taxes communaux dans le cadre des bases et des maxima fixés par la loi des finances." Art. 32: "Le Conseil municipal vote le budget, examine et adopte les comptes de la commune avant leur transmission pour le contrôle de légalité" — establishing state (préfet/tutelle) legality review after council adoption. Art. 79 defines the mayor's role: "préparer et exécuter le budget de la commune dont il est l'ordonnateur; tenir les comptes de la commune; établir les rôles des impôts, taxes et redevances communaux." A 2019 amending law (Loi n°2019-12) exists but was not verified to alter these fiscal articles this round — treat the 2010 text as the base fiscal framework, not confirmed unamended.

reports.title: Directive N°01/2011/CM/UEMOA portant régime financier des collectivités territoriales au sein de l'UEMOA (republished by Niger's Ministère des Finances)
reports.publisher: Conseil des Ministres de l'UEMOA (republished/hosted by Ministère des Finances du Niger)
reports.description: Niger's own Ministry of Finance hosts this WAEMU financial-regime directive on its regulatory page, confirming Niger's MOF distributes it as applicable regulation: page title "Directive N° 01/2011/CM/UEMOA portant régime financier des collectivités territoriales au sein de l'UEMOA" (posted 2017-02-02, 1,639 downloads recorded per the page's own metadata). This is the same WAEMU commune-financial-regime framework already referenced structurally by other WAEMU-country CPI files in this corpus. CAVEAT: only the hosting page's title/metadata was verified this round — the directive's own article-level text was not extracted, since the direct PDF link is gated behind a Joomla/Phocadownload license-agreement wall that blocked both WebFetch and curl retrieval attempts.

reports.title: Réunion du Comité Ministériel de Développement de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), Niamey, 21–25 juillet 2025
reports.description: Niger's own Ministry of Finance, in its own voice, verified via raw HTML extraction: "Le 28 janvier 2024, les trois pays membres de l'AES ont décidé de leur retrait sans délai de la CEDEAO. Dans la même lancée, la réunion des ministres des Etats membres de l'AES tenue à Ouagadougou le 15 février 2024 a proposé une architecture institutionnelle visant notamment à instituer une Confédération entre les trois pays membres. Lors de leur premier sommet tenu à Niamey, le 06 juillet 2024, les Chefs d'Etat des trois pays ont adopté le Traité instituant la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES)." Niger's MOF also hosts a November 2023 "COMMUNIQUE FINAL" from an earlier AES ministerial meeting (metadata-only, full text gated) predating the formal ECOWAS withdrawal.
reports.cadence_note: One-off news/announcement instrument, not a periodic report.

_dropped.edge: Ville de Niamey -> a self-published budget/financial document
_dropped.why: Niamey's own official portal (villedeniamey.ne) was checked across its full navigation, including the only plausibly fiscal-adjacent page (plan-strategique). That 2025-2027 strategic plan contains zero budget figures or financial documents, and itself confirms the post-coup governance disruption: Niamey is now run by an "Administrateur Délégué" (CNSP-appointed) rather than an elected mayor. News coverage (nigerdiaspora.net, lesahel.org) of Conseil de Ville budget sessions exists but is secondary and excluded per the evidence-strict rule. This is a genuine, forced instance of the branch's fallback-to-national-tier rule, and directly supports Thomas's 'collapse of structure' expectation at the municipal level for a country in acute governance disruption.

_dropped.edge: ne-ins-ihpc's own methodology voice -> AFRISTAT (as delegated project manager for the base-2023 IHPC rebasing)
_dropped.why: INS Niger's own site (stat-niger.org/?p=5106) states, in its own voice, that "la Commission de l'Union Economique et Monétaire Ouest Africaine (UEMOA)...a initié et mis en œuvre un Projet de Rénovation de l'Indice (Base 100 en 2023), sous la maitrise d'ouvrage délégué de l'Observatoire Economique et Statistique d'Afrique Subsaharienne (AFRISTAT)." This is a genuine INS-Niger-authored statement naming AFRISTAT's delegated role, but AFRISTAT itself remains unminted (an institution without a titled publication, per this corpus's own standing rule, established in the Mali CPI file).

_dropped.edge: ne-ins-ihpc's own bulletins -> COICOP (as classification nomenclature)
_dropped.why: The term "COICOP" does not appear anywhere in Niger's IHPC bulletins or methodology documents checked this round (full-text search of three separate INS Niger documents). The bulletins use a functional expenditure breakdown structurally consistent with COICOP categories, but INS never names the classification system itself — reported as NOT FOUND rather than inferred, per the evidence-strict rule.

_dropped.why: Both documents are confirmed to exist and be current (their listing pages on finances.gouv.ne give exact titles/dates, and the DPBEP page's own text confirms a dedicated section titled "Situation financière des organismes publics et des Collectivités Territoriales"), but the underlying PDFs are gated behind a Joomla/Phocadownload license-agreement wall that blocked repeated automated retrieval attempts (WebFetch and multiple curl POST variations). The section TITLE is confirmed; its substantive content is NOT FOUND.
